kind: PROCESS VERDICT - the process proving run

rulebookUnderTest.note: DEV_PROCESS.md was four hours old at dispatch and had never been followed by anyone but its author.

prCiFieldsBasis: POSITIVELY EMPTY, not omitted. doc_repo has no CI on doc changes and its commits are planner-owned, so AGENT_CONTRACT 6's PR/SHA/CI minimum has no satisfiable value for any doc_repo lane. Declared empty with basis rather than left absent. That this declaration had to be invented is itself finding PD-1 below.
headlineVerdict: The rulebook HOLDS as a behavioral control and FAILS as a schema. Every one of its behavioral rules that could fire, fired, and each one caught something real - including two errors in the rulebook's own text and one in the lane's own brief. But the close SCHEMA is shaped for a build lane in a code repo, and all three sub-agents had to invent conventions to file a doc_repo close. Structural comparability is therefore PARTIAL, and every divergence traces to schema underspecification rather than to agent behavior.

deliverable1_structuralComparability.verdict: PARTIAL. The three closes are comparable on FINDINGS and non-comparable on ACCOUNTING.
comparable: All three filed valid JSON at the exact dispatched path (AGENT_CONTRACT 6 / DEV_PROCESS 5.1 held 3-for-3).
All three carried rulebookSilentAmbiguousOrWrong and rulebookRulesThatFired in the same shape.
All three carried plannerFiguresChecked and all three found at least one planner figure wrong.
All three left doc_repo edits uncommitted and listed them (AGENT_CONTRACT 6 held 3-for-3).

nonComparableDivergences.divergence: Top-level key count: SA-1=15, SA-3=17, SA-2=24.
nonComparableDivergences.cause: The dispatch named a per-shape minimum key set; the RULEBOOK names one universal minimum written for a build lane. Where the rulebook was silent, each agent extended the schema differently.
nonComparableDivergences.classification: PROCESS DEFECT - schema underspecification. Not an agent defect.

nonComparableDivergences.divergence: PR/CI fields: SA-2 declared them explicitly empty with a stated basis; SA-1 flagged the absence as a rulebook gap and omitted them; SA-3 did not surface them at all.
nonComparableDivergences.cause: AGENT_CONTRACT 6 demands PR numbers, merge SHAs, and CI conclusion strings unconditionally. In a repo with no CI, all three available behaviors are defensible and mutually incomparable: omit (fails a presence check), emit empty (indistinguishable from a build lane that forgot), or annotate (prose in a machine-checkable artifact).
nonComparableDivergences.classification: PROCESS DEFECT - the schema has no shape discriminator.

nonComparableDivergences.divergence: Absence handling: SA-1 needed a state for 'cannot be determined from inside doc_repo' and had no vocabulary for it; SA-2 and SA-3 never hit the case.
nonComparableDivergences.cause: AGENT_CONTRACT 5 distinguishes empty-result from positive-absence but has no state for unobservable-in-scope.
nonComparableDivergences.classification: PROCESS DEFECT - vocabulary gap that pressures agents toward the exact collapse the rule exists to prevent.

nonComparableDivergences.divergence: Edit reporting: SA-2 used a structured `edit` object; SA-1 and SA-3 used flat `filesEdited` arrays.
nonComparableDivergences.cause: Dispatch-driven, not rulebook-driven. The rulebook says only 'list them'.

deliverable1_structuralComparability.shapeJustifiedDifferences: Read-only vs build vs handoff legitimately require different evidence fields (negativeTest exists only for SA-2; recoveryGaps only for SA-3). These are NOT defects and are excluded from the divergence count above.

deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.problem: The rulebook is WRONG AT SOURCE in its own worked example. 1.1 states G0 'had scanned 852 of 1,955 markdown files - 43.6%'. The string '852' appears ZERO times in _inbox/2026-08-14_g0_close.json. That file's own metric 'markdown files scanned repo-wide' is 846, and its text reads '366/846'. The true coverage is 846/1955 = 43.3%, not 43.6%.
deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.propagation: The same wrong figure appears in OPS-17 amendment A-008. Two authoritative documents carry it.
deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.irony: Rule 1.1 exists to stop a number escaping its counting rule. Its own illustrative number did exactly that.
deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.foundBy: SA-2, verified independently by the planner (grep -c '852' -> 0; sed of g0_close lines 429-430 -> 846).
deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.proposedFix: Correct DEV_PROCESS.md:27 and OPS-17 A-008 to '846 of 1,955 - 43.3%'. Operator ruling required (append-only amendment table; DEV_PROCESS 5.4).

deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.problem: The close schema's required minimum ('PR numbers + merge SHAs + CI conclusion strings') is written for a build lane in a code repo. It is structurally unsatisfiable for any doc_repo lane, and it has no affordance for saying so. This is the single largest source of non-comparability measured in this lane.
deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.foundBy: SA-1 and SA-2 independently; predicted by the planner in CP1 before either ran.
deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.proposedFix: Add a required `shape` enum (build | audit | handoff | probe) with the PR/CI block conditionally required, plus a `notApplicable` array so omission becomes a positive declaration. This applies to the schema the same principle AGENT_CONTRACT 5 already applies to data: an empty result is not an absence.

deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.problem: AGENT_CONTRACT 1 says a LANE PLANNER may spawn sub-agents and is entirely SILENT on whether a sub-agent may. The hook forbids nesting as a blanket ruled precondition. One rule, two implementations, disagreeing - the exact CTRL-1 defect class DEV_PROCESS 2.4 was written about, except here the hook is STRICTER than the prose rather than laxer.
deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.evidence: All three G-09 dispatches were blocked; SA-3 required a logged DISPATCH_OVERRIDE (recorded 2026-08-14T18:20:59 in _catalog/dispatch_overrides.log) to execute the shape the operator dispatch ordered.
deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.alsoNoted: AGENT_CONTRACT 1's opening line 'You are a LANE PLANNER... You MAY spawn sub-agents' is compiled VERBATIM into leaf-worker briefs whose first line reads 'Do NOT spawn sub-agents.' Section 1 also carries the CP1/CP2 obligation, which a leaf agent could read as binding on itself.
deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.foundBy: SA-1 and SA-3 independently; pre-registered by the planner in CP1 before the hook fired.
deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.proposedFix: Bound depth explicitly in AGENT_CONTRACT 1: a depth-1 fan from the lane planner is the default; deeper nesting requires a named logged override. Source the hook's depth rule from one data file and add a divergence test, per DEV_PROCESS 2.4. Add role-scoped compilation in scripts/dispatch.mjs so sections 1-2 are marked inapplicable to leaf workers. NOTE: the demonstrated hazard is the ORPHAN, not depth per se - this run supervised its successor and nothing was abandoned.

deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.problem: The absence rule distinguishes empty-result from positive-absence but has no state for a determination that is unobtainable from within the lane's scope. Without that vocabulary the pressure is to collapse it into 'verified absent', which is exactly what the rule exists to prevent.

deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.proposedFix: Add `unobservable-in-scope` as a third state, requiring the agent to name the blocking boundary and who can cross it.

deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.problem: 'Reporting a planner figure as wrong is a successful outcome' creates an incentive to find discrepancies and attaches NO evidentiary standard to doing so. The lane produced THREE bad corrections, all from the SA-3 branch: a manufactured 'A-003 line 32 is off by two' (three independent instruments returned 32; self-retracted by SA-3), a manufactured '_smartsite_masters/ does not exist' (it exists, is tracked with 9 files, and A-008 tracked it deliberately; refuted by the planner), and a wrong citation for the $25,000 price (correct fact, wrong location).
deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.measuredRate: Across the lane, 10 planner-figure corrections were asserted and 7 survived verification. The correction instrument ran 7-for-10.
deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.foundBy: SA-3 caught its successor's; the planner caught SA-3's own. DEV_PROCESS 4.2 worked exactly as designed - each level caught the level below.
deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.proposedFix: A reported planner error must carry the command run and its raw output. Line-number and count corrections require two independent instruments.

deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.problem: Its required fields are all WORKER-STATE-shaped (git status, diffs, branches, PRs) and AGENT_CONTRACT 6's are all CLOSE-ACCOUNTING-shaped. Neither has a slot for WHY THE WORK MEANS WHAT IT MEANS. That is sufficient when a parent recovers its own worker in-thread - it already holds the premise - and insufficient the instant recovery crosses into a fresh context.
deliverable2_rulesSilentAmbiguousOrWrong.evidence: SA-3's successor produced a BUILD card rather than a rendering-pass card ONLY because it independently re-read OPS-17. The handoff artifact did not carry the A-002 BUILD verdict - the entire premise of the lane. It also could not distinguish 'finished' from 'abandoned' (no target item count), and inherited a scope list with G-20 silently omitted.

When an audit finds a control-plane row that is itself WRONG (backlog row 22), 5.4 forbids remediating it, so a known-wrong routing row must be left in place to misroute the next agent. The rule is right about deletions and retirements but has no fast path for a factual correction to a pointer.
A spawning sub-agent inherits the CP1/CP2 obligation but its dispatch names no CP paths, so there is no defined location for a sub-lane's checkpoints.
